title: Run rule for a halt instruction
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, and let $\rho$ be a register assignment, $p$ an input position, and $\ell\in\Lambda$ a label. If the instruction at $\ell$ is to halt, then for every output string $o$, the program reaches the halted state with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ within at most one step.
hypotheses_covered: The claim holds for every initial output string $o$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$ and $\ell$ a label whose
instruction is $\mathsf{halt}$.  Then for all registers $\rho$ and input
positions $p$, from label $\ell$ with registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the
program reaches the halted state, with registers still $\rho$ and still $p$
symbols read, within one step and without printing anything.
